method: DEM column collapse of coarse-grained salt with pendular liquid bridges (Willett 2000 capillary force), dry vs two liquid contents
notes: Ran as intended at reduced scale (diameters coarse-grained x4, N=1200, 0.4 s after release). Marked partial because the dry baseline has no rolling resistance on a smooth floor and spreads into a monolayer, so no repose angle could be measured. The trend with liquid content is clear, but the dry-to-wet contrast is larger than real salt would show. Yade's ViscEl rolling resistance is viscous as coded (M = -mR*|Fn|*omega_rel), so mR was set to 0. Only the W=1% case was at rest at the 0.4 s cap; the dry runout is a lower bound (grains still rolling), and W=0.1% was still creeping (KE 8e-7 J).
